findings.title: join() can skip terminating flusher workers when the deadline has expired
findings.body: SpanFlusher.join() computes a deadline, joins next_step with the full timeout, then iterates over worker processes. If the deadline has already passed, remaining_time <= 0 executes break, exiting the loop before any terminate() calls. If the deadline expires while waiting for one worker, subsequent workers are also never terminated. In addition, deadline = time.time() + timeout if timeout else None treats timeout=0 as no timeout, so a zero timeout can block indefinitely. During shutdown or rebalance this can leave flusher processes running or hang shutdown.

findings.title: --flusher-processes is not validated as a positive integer
findings.body: The new --flusher-processes option accepts any int. In SpanFlusher.__init__, max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards) makes 0 silently mean 'use one process per shard' rather than zero, and a negative value makes num_processes negative; with non-empty assigned shards, the subsequent modulo assignment into an empty process_to_shards_map raises KeyError during consumer startup. The option should use a positive-int validator or explicitly define the behavior for zero.

findings.title: Crashed flusher workers are only restarted when a new message is submitted
findings.body: poll() only delegates to next_step.poll(); process liveness is checked only from submit() via _ensure_processes_alive(). If a flusher process dies while the consumer is idle or no new span batches arrive, it will not be restarted until the next submit. Since the flusher is responsible for expiring and flushing buffered segments in the background, this can leave segments stuck in Redis indefinitely on idle partitions.

findings.title: Unhealthy flusher workers can be replaced without ensuring the old worker is stopped
findings.body: In _ensure_processes_alive(), a worker considered hung is killed only if it is a multiprocessing.Process, and the replacement is created immediately without joining or reaping the old worker. In the produce_to_pipe path the worker is a threading.Thread, which cannot be killed; if it was only temporarily hung, the old and replacement workers can flush the same shards concurrently, potentially producing duplicate segments and calling done_flush_segments concurrently. Even for processes, repeatedly killing without joining can leak zombie processes or file descriptors.

findings.title: test_basic waits using a sleep that has been monkeypatched to a no-op
findings.body: test_basic monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op, then later calls time.sleep(0.1) to give flusher threads time to process after advancing current_drift. Because the sleep is patched out, there is no real wait or synchronization before step.join() sets the stopped flag. This leaves a race where the flusher may stop before flushing the expected message, making the test potentially flaky.
